framework: Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS), English Language Arts and Reading — Fluency strand
citation: TEKS ELAR §110.3–110.7, knowledge-and-skills statement 4 (grades 1–5): "use appropriate fluency (rate, accuracy, and prosody) when reading grade-level text." Kindergarten (§110.2) has no standalone fluency standard; the K–2 band includes its precursor skills.
prosodyNote: This project splits TEKS 'prosody' into two trackable components: expression and phrasing.

rate.description: Reading at a pace that supports understanding — not too slow, not racing.

bands.K-2: Move from word-by-word reading toward smooth, sentence-level reading of decodable and grade-level text.
bands.3-5: Read grade-level text at a conversational pace, adjusting speed for difficulty and purpose.

accuracy.description: Reading words correctly, using decoding and context to self-correct.

bands.K-2: Accurately decode regularly spelled words and recognize high-frequency words.
bands.3-5: Read grade-level text with few errors, self-correcting using context and word structure.

expression.description: Reading with a voice that matches the meaning — tone, emphasis, and end-mark intonation.

bands.K-2: Notice end punctuation and begin to change voice for questions and exclamations.
bands.3-5: Read dialogue and narration with tone and emphasis that reflect the author's meaning.

phrasing.description: Grouping words into meaningful chunks and pausing at punctuation instead of reading word-by-word.

bands.K-2: Move from finger-pointed word-by-word reading to short meaningful phrases.
bands.3-5: Read in longer phrases, using commas and clause boundaries to guide pauses.
